# C10 — Mediation / Pramāṇa

## #0

Within the essay’s argued whole, **pramāṇa is Objective Internality as means**, between Subjective Immediacy as knower and World as known; Life / Mind is the whole relation. [C41](C41-Objective-Internality.md) defines that constituted interior. C10 specifies how a particular disclosure occurs and what can warrant it. This native appointment does not make every operation of an internality a valid cognition by virtue of its occurrence; a report, inference or model retains the warrant proper to its mode.

Mediation is the determinate means through which a claim, perception or relation becomes available. The means belongs to what must be understood about the disclosure: how it reaches its object, what it makes salient, what it transforms and under what conditions it fails. Knowledge remains possible under the formal limit because availability does not require possession of the source.

[C05 — Immutable Gap](C05-Immutable-Gap.md) **grounds** this condition. C10 follows its positive consequence: the gap demands an account of the relation through which something is known. *Pramāṇa* names a source-specific Indian epistemological neighbour concerning means of valid cognition. Its validity conditions require their own recovery; the term cannot silently certify every language, instrument or model that mediates.

## #1

[[symbolon/episteme/sources/indian-philosophy/dyczkowski/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration.md|Dyczkowski — The Doctrine of Vibration]] **sources** a determinate Śaiva articulation in the locally held discussion, pp.63–64. Subject, object and means of knowledge attend the cognitive act together. The means is not a neutral addition inserted after an independently complete subject and object have been established. Their differentiation belongs to the one act whose articulation makes an object available.

The three luminaries preserve that relation as an image. The Sun figures the illuminating means, the Moon the object shining by reflected light, and Fire the subject which takes the perceived into itself. These are Dyczkowski's account of Śaiva symbolism. They expose a relational operation; their use does not establish a universal pramāṇa taxonomy or make QL a borrowed Śaiva doctrine.

## #2

The relation must preserve the difference it renders intelligible. Dyczkowski's pp.65–66 press this through colour: if consciousness were entirely homogeneous in its knowing, blue and yellow could not appear as distinct. Formless availability and determinate appearance must be thought together. At pp.70–72, the distinction between a mirror or crystal and conscious reflexivity adds an active power of recognition, memory and presentation to the account. A mechanically reflected appearance does not by itself supply that whole operation.

[A05 — Prakāśa / Vimarśa](../A05-Prakasa-Vimarsa.md) **grounds** the illumination/reflexivity movement. C10 retains its epistemic middle: disclosure has a mode, and the mode participates in how the disclosed becomes knowable. The source's claims about consciousness remain in their Śaiva register; a computational system's memory or self-description requires its own operational demonstration.

## #3

A symbol makes the same demand on an account. [[symbolon/episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-definition-god-draft3/taylor-2026-definition-god-draft3.md|Taylor — Definition of God, Draft3]] **grounds** the authorial movement in which an unavailable whole nevertheless orders its partial expressions. Its image of iron filings patterned around a magnet makes mediation legible: the pattern answers to a relation whose source it does not contain. The image carries the operation without turning magnetic physics into proof of the whole argument.

A determinate sign fixes something; a living symbol carries that determination in a relation exceeding it. [C09 — Diaphaneity](C09-Diaphaneity.md) **extends** this into reading the shaping conditions through what appears. [A06 — Vāk](../A06-Vak.md) **extends** it through articulation: speech is one developed mediation, while feeling, perception, intention, contact and attention prevent mediation from being restricted to fully formed verbal statements.

## #4

An account therefore distinguishes source, means and warrant. Perception, remembered presentation, testimony, inference, instrument and model cannot acquire one another's authority simply by delivering the same sentence. A model-generated claim that reproduces an available source and a model-generated conjecture have different relations to what they assert. The source must remain recoverable, and the transformation must be intelligible enough to assess its consequence.

The [Sanskrit enumeration case](../../../symbolon/episteme/etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md#sanskrit-enumeration-and-discriminative-practice) **historicises** a distinct pramāṇa taxonomy: Kārikās 4–6 distinguish perception, inference and trustworthy testimony. At register 3, C10 receives the requirement to retain which means warranted this claim. This acquired Sāṃkhya case supplements the Śaiva discussion without making either school’s taxonomy universal.

[[symbolon/episteme/etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/WHOLE-FIELD|Symbol / Account / Trust]] **grounds** this register3 operation: the account states how it answers to source. [C29 — Mediating Office](C29-Mediating-Office-Derivative-Sovereignty.md) **qualifies** the neighbouring authority problem. C10 concerns how something is known; C29 concerns the office authorised to act or speak. An office can carry an epistemic means without becoming either its source or its guarantee.

## #5→0

The return is practical. [A31 — Deferential Intelligence](../A31-Deferential-Intelligence.md) **tests** whether the means and its evaluator can be revised by encounter. The direct quilt's changed-economy proposal makes this exact: a search can vary its answers indefinitely while leaving untouched the model and standard by which an answer counts. An answerable mediation retains source, exclusions, disagreement, limit and a route through which the account itself can change.

[C48 — Trust / Faith](C48-Trust-Faith-under-Formal-Limit.md) **extends** the resulting reliance. Trust acts through an account whose source exceeds it; it does not wait for mediation to vanish. C10 **returns-to** [C08 — Context Frame](C08-Context-Context-Frame.md), where the means is situated, and C09, where its determining relation becomes readable. What is learned through a means can then revise how the means is used.

**Depth Restoration:** the subject–object–means act, Sun/Moon/Fire image, differentiated colour and active reflexivity, symbolic source relation, epistemic means/authorised office distinction and revisable evaluator are restored.

**Unresolved Delta:** Dyczkowski supplies a particular Śaiva account, not school-by-school pramāṇa taxonomies. The local transcript reaches p.81; selected-edition quotation collation remains pending, and this page paraphrases it. The technical return is an argued requirement, not a completed experiment. Other schools' validity criteria require their own source recovery before addition.
